scopes.A0: Rule arithmetic: fixed-nest rule S_N(M)=M(N+1)^2/N, rational fibres, lattices. No interaction or continuation choice.
scopes.A1: SELECT-I anchor-route model: routes r=(k,d), v=kd^2, joint operations J on routes.
scopes.A2: SELECT-II declared self-iteration graph: integer values, edge m -> m(N+1)^2/N for N|m (a chosen substitution convention).
scopes.R: G1-R route-aware pair interaction *_j (a chosen grammar; uses labels).
scopes.C: G1-C collective map C(x)=x+L^2/G (a chosen grammar; label-blind, non-stationary).
scopes.X: Statement about the choice itself (axioms for interactions, nonselection, incompatibility).
scopes.MIXED: Compound record: each part is tagged [A0], [C], [X] ... in the statement; the parts have different scopes.

records.title: Selection = reachability order
records.stmt: A commutative-associative-idempotent J is the lub of the order J(r,s)=s; conversely every such order with lubs gives such a J. Selecting J is selecting a reachability order.
records.hyp: Model of anchor routes; standard semilattice fact.

records.title: Coordinate rigidity
records.stmt: If f(q(N+1)-1)=q f(N) for all primes q then f=c(N+1). J_N and J_occ are not covariant (failures 10088/11737 and 10306/11737 on tested pairs).
records.hyp: Coordinate chart question: which chart is homogeneous under T_q.
records.proof: Short proof in note; finite checks listed.
records.corr: Caveat in source: rigidity says which chart is homogeneous under T_q, not why UNNS must require covariance.

records.title: Amplification order and J_join
records.stmt: With amplification moves E_{p,k}, E_{p,d} only: r<=s iff k|k' and d|d'; the lub is J_join. 'Conditional Selection Theorem' is true but definitional.
records.hyp: E (amplification as a generative step) is a HYPOTHESIS, generated neither by the nest rule nor by T_q.
records.proof: lub proved; brute force on 144 pairs.

records.title: Minimality from absorption
records.stmt: For a semilattice J: retention <=> <=_J subset <=_E; absorption <=> <=_E subset <=_J. Together <=_J = <=_E, hence J=J_join. 'Least' is derived from absorption, not an extra axiom.
records.hyp: Semilattice J on routes; order <=_E from S1.3.

records.title: Fork: refinement as a generative step
records.stmt: If T_q is also a generative step, the least common continuation is J_ref(r,s)=(lcm(v_r,v_s)/L^2, L), L=lcm(d_r,d_s); v(J_ref)=lcm(v_r,v_s) so it separates NO fibre (1277 same-value pairs, m<=3000). With inverse refinements as steps, minimal continuations are the whole fibre F(lcm(v_r,v_s)) (122/144 pairs have >1).
records.hyp: T_q treated as a step (not as a symmetry). The separation theorem of the manuscript (sec. 11) holds exactly when T_q is a symmetry/equivalence.

records.title: Nest iteration consumes the factor N
records.stmt: Iterating the nest rule on its own value m (N|m) gives m'=(m/N)(N+1)^2; m|m' only for N=1 (m'=4m).
records.hyp: Checked m<=2000. Source flags the reading ('natural nest iteration') as a reading, not a finding about canonical UNNS.

records.title: Discrimination matrix of joint operations
records.stmt: Algebra + covariance admit six operations (J_join, J_max, J_min, J_lexmax, J_ref, J_mixB); adding retention leaves only J_join. J_N and J_occ are associative; J_mul separates nothing (not idempotent); J_max satisfies absorption, so absorption alone does not select J_join.
records.hyp: Finite box k<=10, d<=10, fibres m<=1500, grid 24x24. 26 checks pass, 4 DATA rows.

records.title: SELECT-I verdict (S5)
records.stmt: Factor-preserving least continuation is not an intrinsic consequence of nesting and refinement; it is an additional rule (a reachability order). Regime-dependent family: J_join (relationally rich) vs J_ref (value-level, no fibre separation).
records.hyp: Frozen release v1.0.0 (21 Oct 2026). Statements concern the anchor-route model only; broader UNNS grammar, physics, field occurrences and entanglement remain open.

records.title: Out-degree, growth and acyclicity
records.stmt: Each m has exactly tau(m) distinct successors (one per N|m); t/m=N+2+1/N>=4 (=4 only for N=1); the graph is acyclic; m|t iff N=1.
records.hyp: Declared self-iteration convention m -> m(N+1)^2/N, integer successors only.

records.title: In-degree equals nest multiplicity
records.stmt: indegree(t)=R(t)=#{d>=2 : d^2|t}=prod_p(floor(nu_p(t)/2)+1)-1; sources are exactly the squarefree integers; every integer has a squarefree ancestor; ancestor chains have length <= log_4 t.
records.hyp: Same convention as S2.1.

records.title: Edge label is identifiable
records.stmt: For an edge m=kN -> t=k(N+1)^2: gcd(m,t)=k, N=m/gcd(m,t); the edge test is exact from the two values.
records.hyp: Same convention.

records.title: No universal least common future
records.stmt: The values 1 and 2 have exactly {81,100} as common futures up to 100; 81 does not reach 100; hence no least common future: the reachability order is not a join-semilattice.
records.hyp: Specific pair; explicit paths 1-4-18-81, 2-8-81, 1-4-16-100, 2-9-100.
records.corr: Not a counterexample to RGG-2's join theorem, which concerns a different (factor-amplification) order.

records.title: Occurrence = edge; fibre multiplicity = in-degree
records.stmt: The generated occurrence (M,N), N|M, is the edge M -> M(N+1)^2/N; the anchor route (k,d) in F(t) is the incoming edge from m=k(d-1) with N=d-1. Route distinctness within a value fibre is predecessor distinctness (checked t<=5000).
records.hyp: Same convention.
records.proof: In note; dictionary between SELECT-I/FIELD-I and SELECT-II objects.

records.title: Fixed-target reachability is decidable
records.stmt: Whether m reaches t is decided by finite bounded traversal (edges strictly increase).
records.hyp: Same convention.

records.title: Joins and meets fail (counts)
records.stmt: 1 and 2 have 21 minimal common successors <=20000. Pairs 1<=a<b<=40: 23 comparable, 702 with >=2 minimal common successors (certified no join). Pairs 2<=a<b<400: 77916 have no common ancestor, 660 a unique maximal one, 53 >=2 maximal (e.g. (32,300): {2,6}); the order is neither join- nor meet-semilattice.
records.hyp: Exact finite counts (truncation noted in source for 15 pairs).
records.proof: Exact finite enumeration; 12 checks pass, 3 DATA rows.

records.title: J_join is not an intrinsic reachability object
records.stmt: The manuscript join value v(r v r')=t(L/g)^2 is reachable from t in 72 of 112 tested fibre pairs (t<400) and a common successor of both predecessors in 76. J_join is not recovered from intrinsic reachability.
records.hyp: Data, explicitly not a theorem about all fibres.

records.title: Backward recurrence for reachability
records.stmt: m reaches t iff m=t or some predecessor p of t is reached from m. Every path m ~> t has at most floor(log_4(t/m)) edges.
records.hyp: Same convention. Checked against forward search on all 1,125,750 pairs 1<=m<=t<=1500 and 60 random pairs up to 10^5.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: No shortcuts: every edge is a cover relation
records.stmt: If p -> t is an edge, t is not reachable from p by any path of two or more edges. Hence the graph is the Hasse diagram of the reachability order; the predecessors of any t form an antichain; every confluence is minimal.
records.hyp: Proof via phi(d)=d^2/(d-1) in lowest terms. Checked p<3000, t<=10^6.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: Path length is not a rank function
records.stmt: 6 ~> 784 has paths of length 2 and 3: the graph is not graded.
records.hyp: Single exact example.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: History counts H(t)
records.stmt: H(t)>=max(1,R(t)); for non-sources H(t)=R(t) iff every predecessor has exactly one history. H(72)=4 versus R(72)=3. Tower value -> route -> history is strict at each level (data to 5000: 5000 values, 3124 routes, 8283 histories).
records.hyp: Recurrence confirmed against explicit enumeration t<=3000; counts t<=20000 are DATA (7840 non-sources, H>R for 1309, smallest t=64, max H=275 at t=16200).
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: Markov no-go for continuation
records.stmt: Continuations of a history depend only on its endpoint, so any joint operation defined by extension with the merge endpoint as observation depends on endpoints only; the set deficit of Theorem 11.9 is 0. Routes or histories can never be told apart by continuation in this graph.
records.hyp: Checked on all endpoints t<400 with >=2 histories (44 endpoints, depth 3).
records.proof: Immediate from the graph definition; implementation checked.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: J_pred separates automatically (leakage)
records.stmt: For probe r, J_pred(r,r)={p} equals J_pred(s,r) iff s's predecessor reaches p; by the antichain property (S2.10) this never happens, so J_pred separates every fibre pair (1277/1277, t<=3000). This is leakage (the inputs differ), not continuation information.
records.hyp: Uses S2.10.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: Intrinsic confluence of fibre routes
records.stmt: For routes r,r' in F(t) with predecessors p,p', t is always a minimal common successor of p,p' (1277/1277). A second incomparable minimal merge below t occurs for 9/1277 pairs (t=784: {432,784}; t=1089: {648,1089}; t=1568: {864,1568}) -- DATA.
records.hyp: The 9-pair pattern is observed in three examples only.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: SELECT-II verdict
records.stmt: The only intrinsic route/history information in the nest graph is retrospective (ancestry, merge structure); forward continuation never exposes it. A history-sensitive relational operation needs a backward-reading definition, and then separation is automatic. Neither J_join nor J_ref is intrinsic; any single-valued joint operation needs an additional selection principle (consistent with SELECT-I).
records.hyp: Statement about the declared self-iteration graph only.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence (with v002a)

records.title: Rational-Fibre Theorem
records.stmt: For reduced x=a/b, occurrences of x correspond to {d>=2 : d^2|a, d=1 mod b}; N=d-1, M=(a/d^2)(d-1)/b.
records.hyp: Positive rationals; fixed-nest rule S_N(M)=M(N+1)^2/N.
records.proof: Elementary (gcd(d^2,d-1)=1). Brute force on 109,557 reduced a/b.

records.title: Reparametrisation
records.stmt: M=kg, N=bg, gcd(k,b)=1 gives value k(bg+1)^2/b in lowest terms; denominator b=N/gcd(M,N).

records.title: Sub-fibre form
records.stmt: F(a/b) = {anchors of a with b|N} via (M,N)->(bM,N); hence R(a/b)<=R(a).

records.title: Lattice lcm (Lemma 0)
records.stmt: For reduced p/q, p'/q': (p/q)Z cap (p'/q')Z = (lcm(p,p')/gcd(q,q'))Z.
records.hyp: Z-modules of rationals.

records.title: Cross-nest intersection
records.stmt: S_N1(Z>0) cap S_N2(Z>0) = {jL^2/g}, L=lcm(N1+1,N2+1), g=gcd(N1,N2); gcd(g,L)=1, so the first coincidence is an integer iff gcd(N1,N2)=1.
records.proof: Lattice lcm of reduced lattices (Lemma 0 is stated in v002).

records.title: Realisability
records.stmt: A non-integer a/b is realised iff a has a square divisor d^2, d>1, d=1 mod b; necessary a>=(b+1)^2, tight (=S_b(1)).

records.title: Congruence obstruction (original form)
records.stmt: d,d' in D(a/b): lcm(d,d') in D(a/b) iff gcd(d,d')=1 mod b. Smallest failure x=400/3, d=4, d'=10.
records.hyp: Original gcd clause omitted the exclusion d>=2.
records.corr: Corrected by F.T16 (v002): gcd(d,d') in D iff gcd>=2 and gcd=1 mod b.

records.title: Refinement preserves the rational fibre
records.stmt: T_q:(k,d)->(k/q^2,dq) preserves the rational fibre iff q=1 mod b.

records.title: Rendezvous x+L^2/gcd(N,N') (v001 observation)
records.stmt: Two same-value occurrences first re-coincide at x+L^2/gcd(N,N') (checked 5394 pairs). It depends on labels (N,N'), not on the manuscript distance D (22 of 44 D-values carry >1 rendezvous).
records.hyp: Proposed in v001; proved as T6 in v002.
records.corr: Superseded by F.T6.

records.title: Common future of a pair
records.stmt: For r,s in F(x), the common values at or after x are exactly x+j*Delta, j>=0, Delta=L^2/g (L=lcm(d,d'), g=gcd(N,N')).
records.proof: Lattice lcm of the two routes' reduced steps.

records.title: Integrality of the rendezvous index
records.stmt: h_rs=x/Delta_rs=(a/L^2)(g/b) is a positive integer; x < x_next <= 2x.

records.title: Collective rendezvous, coherence, gamma=gcd H
records.stmt: (a) Common future of all of F(x) is x+j*Delta_coll, Delta_coll=lcm(d_i^2)/gcd(N_i). (b) Delta_coll is the lattice-lcm of the pairwise Delta_rs. (c) gamma(x)=x/Delta_coll is a positive integer and equals gcd H(x).
records.hyp: R(x)>=2 for the gcd statement.

records.title: Every positive integer is a pair index
records.stmt: For x=36h, d=2 and d'=3 lie in D(x), L=6, g=1, Delta=36, h_rs=h.

records.title: Rigidity of the labelled structure
records.stmt: (a) r->(v(r),v(Fr)) is injective, so the labelled regime carries exactly (M,N). (b) The structure (Occ,v,route-membership) has trivial automorphism group: retaining route membership makes 'relational' information coincide with label information. Label-blind structure is value-level, with automorphism group Pi.
records.hyp: Checked N<400 for route-value-set distinctness.

records.title: Regime A / orbit lemma
records.stmt: Pi acts transitively on unordered pairs of every fibre with R>=2; a Pi-invariant function of an unordered pair is a function of the fibre alone.

records.title: Admissible family (non-selection from A1-A3)
records.stmt: A1-A3 hold for a pair operation iff *(r,s)=x+j(r,s)Delta_rs with j in Z>0. Adding A4 requires j constant on tau-orbits; constant maps j=1,2,3,... and others satisfy A1-A4 and differ on every pair. A7 (minimality) selects j=1 and is independent of A1-A4.
records.hyp: Axioms A1-A7 as in the v002 SPEC / G1-G3 memo (A2 symmetry, A3 common future, A4 stationarity, A6 label-blindness, A7 minimality).

records.title: Label-blind operations are collective
records.stmt: A value-valued * with A2,A3,A6 satisfies *(r,s)=Y(x)=x+j(x)Delta_coll(x)=x(1+j(x)/gamma(x)), j(x) in Z>0 free. With A7: Y_1(x)=x(1+1/gamma(x)).
records.corr: Wording 'only gamma matters' is clarified by the v003 erratum (see F.E3).

records.title: No label-blind occurrence-valued operation
records.stmt: There is no Pi-equivariant operation assigning to each pair an occurrence at a value y>x on both routes (it would be fixed by Sym(F(y)), forcing |F(y)|=1).

records.title: Incompatibility of stationarity and label-blindness
records.stmt: No pair operation on the full domain satisfies A3, A4 and A6 together (in the G1-G3 memo: A3, A4 and the weaker A6w).
records.hyp: Full domain Dom only; value-valued outputs; A6w is the weak form. Restricting the domain or the shifts, fibre-valued outputs, or invariance under a proper subgroup of Pi are NOT covered.
records.proof: Proof by choosing primes p>max(g,L), p=1 mod g, p^2 | numerator (Dirichlet).
records.corr: Scope sharpened in the G1-G3 memo (Theorem I; hypotheses actually used listed there).

records.title: Join on rational fibres (corrected T4)
records.stmt: For d,d' in D(a/b): lcm in D iff gcd(d,d')=1 mod b; gcd in D iff gcd>=2 and gcd=1 mod b. If b=1, D(m) is closed under lcm; if b>1 the join may fail (x=400/3, D={4,10}).
records.corr: Corrects F.T4.

records.title: Theorem N (nonselection among A2+A3 operations)
records.stmt: A2+A3 are satisfied exactly by *(r,s)=x+j(r,s)Delta_rs; the R-family (constant j) satisfies A2,A3,A4 and fails A6; the C-family Y_j satisfies A2,A3,A6 and fails A4; *_1 and C coincide on two-route fibres (488/1116 corpus fibres, data) and differ on 1340/3642 pairs with R>=3 (data). A7 is independent of A1-A4.
records.proof: Proved in memo; corpus counts are DATA.

records.title: Theorem I (A3+A4+A6w incompatible)
records.stmt: There is no *:Dom->Q satisfying A3, A4 and A6w (hence none satisfying A3, A4, A6). A2 is not used.
records.hyp: See scope list in memo sec. 4 (full domain, value-valued, weak A6w).
records.proof: Proof in memo; counterexample data x=36 pair (2,3), p=7,11,13,...

records.title: G1-R route-aware pair interaction
records.stmt: r *_j s = x+j*Delta(r,s), j>=1 (constant on tau-orbits). A2,A3,A4; excludes A6/A6w.
records.hyp: A grammar choice, not forced by the rule.

records.title: G1-C collective map C
records.stmt: C(x)=x+Delta_coll(x)=x(1+1/gamma(x))=x+L^2/G, with D(x)={d>=2: d^2|a, d=1 mod b}, G=gcd{d-1}, L=lcm D. Iteration x_{k+1}=C(x_k). A2,A3,A6,A7c; fails A4 (Theorem I).
records.hyp: CHOSEN interaction (nonselection theorem F.GN/F.T12). All Volume II results are consequences of this map; none concerns other UNNS grammars.
records.proof: Definition; D(x)<=D(C(x)) proved in memo (G.6). Mathematical dependency is only the arithmetic of Delta_coll (F.T8); F.GN, F.GI, F.T12, F.T13 are the MOTIVATION for choosing C and are deliberately not listed as dependencies.

records.title: Delta_coll is reduced
records.stmt: Delta_coll=lcm(d_i^2)/G is in lowest terms.
records.proof: p|G divides every N_i, so p does not divide any d_j.

records.title: Plateau law
records.stmt: D(x_{n+1}) contains D(x_n); while D is unchanged, x_{n0+k}=(gamma_0+k)u/v.

records.title: Growth-time bound
records.stmt: For realised x and integer d>=2 not in D(x): 1<=K_d<=v d^2-1 and T(x)<=K_d; T(x)<=G(x)d_min^2-1.

records.title: Collective fibre growth
records.stmt: For realised x_0 (R>=1), R(x_n) is non-decreasing, R(x_n)->infinity and the union of D(x_n) is infinite. No infinite constant-multiplicity plateau; no growth rate is claimed.
records.hyp: Conditional on adopting C.

records.title: Integer R=3 fibres are non-rigid
records.stmt: A 3-element divisor/lcm-closed subset of N>=2 is {p,q,pq} or {p,p^2,p^3}; each has a non-trivial weighted-triangle automorphism.
records.hyp: b=1 (integer values).

records.title: Rigid rational R=3 example
records.stmt: x=20736/5 has D={6,16,36}, pair indices {1,9,16}: a rigid three-route graph; the only rational R=3 fibre in the searched range (a<=40000, b<=40, 371 fibres).
records.hyp: v003 left the classification of rational R=3 fibres open; shapes are classified by F.T24, rigidity by F.T29, infinite families by F.T25; the full list of primitive configurations remains open (O4.1).

records.title: Erratum: 'only gamma matters' (v003)
records.stmt: gamma determines the admissible set x+Delta_coll Z>0; the selection j(x) may depend on any value-level invariant or none (Y=2x). v002 files are intentionally unedited.
records.corr: Corrects the wording of v002 RESULTS.md.

records.title: Reduction to the square-root part
records.stmt: With a=s^2 t (t squarefree): D(a/b)={d|s : d>=2, d=1 mod b}; the fibre depends only on (s,b); h_ij=t*H0; every fibre has a primitive representative (lambda,b). Squarefree scaling: D(ma/b)=D(a/b) for squarefree m coprime to ab.

records.title: Closure lemmas (Q), (G)
records.stmt: (Q) d|e in D implies e/d is 1 or in D. (G) d,e in D with gcd=1 mod b imply lcm in D, gcd 1 or in D.

records.title: Shape theorem for three-route fibres (b>=2)
records.stmt: Exactly one of: chain {q,q^2,q^3} (non-rigid); lambda d3=d1d2 (non-rigid); V (impossible); one comparable pair {q,q^2,e} (always rigid); antichain (rigid iff three weights distinct).
records.hyp: b>=2 (for b=1 antichain and one-pair shapes cannot occur: F.T20).

records.title: Infinite rigid families
records.stmt: (a) scaled families from any rigid primitive (s,b) with squarefree t coprime to b; (b) b=3, s=22r, r prime, r=23 mod 63 gives D={22,2r,11r}, rigid (Dirichlet).

records.title: Exact global minimum of the growth-time bound
records.stmt: The minimum of K_d over d not in D is attained by finite search d<=floor(sqrt((gamma+k0)/v)).

records.title: Provable lower bound for growth of R
records.stmt: (a) G(x_n) is non-increasing along C-orbits; (b) d_min<=R+2, hence T(x)<=v0(R+2)^2-1 and R(x_n) >~ (3n/v0)^(1/3). Weak: sampled orbits grow much faster.

records.title: Monotone fibre growth is specific to the collective branch
records.stmt: Along route-aware orbits D need not grow: x=36, pair (2,3): R(36(k+1))=3,3,3,5,3,3,3,5 (R drops 5 to 3 at x=180); 118/118 pair orbits show a decrease in the first 10 steps (data).

records.title: Signature criterion for three-route rigidity
records.stmt: w(d,e)=g/L^2 is in lowest terms (gcd(g,L)=1); w=w' iff (L,g)=(L',g'). A three-route fibre is rigid iff its three signatures (L_ij,g_ij) are pairwise distinct.
records.proof: Proved. Closes problem J1 of v004.

records.title: Arithmetic of G
records.stmt: (a) b|G(x); (b) gcd(u(D),G)=1 so Delta_coll=u/G is reduced; (c) G(x)=1 iff 2 in D(x) iff x is an integer divisible by 4.
records.hyp: D(x) nonempty.

records.title: Monotone orbits
records.stmt: D(x_n) is contained in D(x_{n+1}) and G_{n+1}|G_n.

records.title: Regime I: closed dynamics for G=1
records.stmt: For integer x=s^2 t divisible by 4: D={d|s,d>=2}, G=1, Delta_coll=s^2, C(x)=s^2(t+1)=s'^2 t'; t->sqf(t+1) is absorbed into the cycle 1->2->3->1 and s doubles every three steps; R(x_n)=tau(s_n)-1.

records.title: Non-universality of reach
records.stmt: For every collective orbit the reach set U=union D(x_n) omits infinitely many d>=2. (A) if G_inf>1, U contains only d=1 mod G_inf (2 never reached); (B) if G_inf=1, the orbit is eventually in regime I and U={d>=2: d | s_N 2^k}.
records.hyp: Non-universality holds for all orbits; the O(log X) counting/density-0 claim holds only when the orbit reaches G=1.
records.corr: Scope erratum F.L5 (v006): density statement requires G_inf=1; for G_inf=g>1 only upper density <=1/g is proved there; F.T40 closes P_g.

records.title: G=2 cannot persist
records.stmt: If G(x)=2, G collapses to 1 in at most 7 further steps.

records.title: Modular escape from any fixed fibre
records.stmt: If G(x)=g>1 and the fibre were unchanged under repeated C, then y_k=gx_k=y_0+kL^2 reaches 0 mod 4g (L odd, k<=4g) or mod g (L even, k<=g), forcing G=1. Hence the orbit must acquire an additional modulus no later than that k.

records.title: Universal collapse for G=2,3,6
records.stmt: G=2 collapses within 7 steps; G=3 within 2; G=6 within 29. A permanently stabilised G_inf cannot equal 2, 3 or 6.

records.title: Exact eventual three-step scaling in regime I
records.stmt: For G=1: x_{n+3}=4x_n, gamma(x_n)=t_n in {1,2,3}, s_{n+3}=2s_n, R(x_{n+3})-R(x_n)=tau(o), o=odd part of s_N.
records.hyp: G=1 (regime I only).

records.title: Exact reach counting for G=1
records.stmt: U(X)=sum_{q|o,q<=X}(1+floor(log_2(X/q)))-1; density zero.
records.hyp: G=1 branch.

records.title: Scope erratum to v005 T33
records.stmt: The O(log X) / density-0 conclusion of T33 needs G_inf=1; for hypothetical G_inf=g>1 only upper density <=1/g is proved. Non-universality itself stands.
records.corr: Corrects F.T33 (scope).

records.title: Full collapse to G=1 (problem)
records.stmt: Whether every realised initial value reaches G=1.
records.corr: Settled NEGATIVELY by F.T39 (v007): persistent regimes exist.

records.title: Transition criterion
records.stmt: d in D(x') iff d^2|Y and g/gcd(g,d-1) | Y/d^2 (Y=y+L^2). Event classes: none / preserving / reducing; G(x')=gcd(g,{d-1: d new}).

records.title: Anatomy of a preserving event
records.stmt: New moduli are coprime to g, divide no part of L, contain a fresh prime (q^2 | y+L^2) or a carried prime power; N is divisor-closed.

records.title: Plateau escape
records.stmt: Between two growth events a G>1 orbit spends <=4g steps (L odd) or <=g (L even); a persistent orbit has infinitely many growth events, all preserving after some time.

records.title: Persistent regime P_g (counterexample to collapse)
records.stmt: For g>=5, gcd(g,6)=1, s=2^k m with (H1)-(H3): x_n=s_n^2 t_n/g with t_n in {1,2,3}, G(x_n)=g, x_{n+3}=4x_n for all n; the orbit never reaches G=1.
records.hyp: Hypotheses H1-H3 as stated in source; existence via T38a.
records.corr: gcd(g,6)=1 requirement was too strong: see F.T46.

records.title: Existence of P_g for every such g
records.stmt: Take q the least odd prime = 2 mod g (Dirichlet), o=ord_g(2), m=w q^o: (H1)-(H3) hold.
records.proof: Proved. Instances g=5,7,11,13,17,19,23,25,29,35,49,55,65,77 by direct iteration.
records.corr: Elementary version without Dirichlet: F.T42.

records.title: Universal G-collapse is false
records.stmt: There are collective orbits with G(x_n)=g>1 for every n, for every g>=5 coprime to 6. Settles K3.6 (v005) and L6 negatively.
records.corr: Its remark 'P needs gcd(g,6)=1' is superseded by F.T46.

records.title: Reach set and growth in P_g
records.stmt: In P_g: U={d>=2: d | s_N 2^k, d=1 mod g}; counting function O(log X); R(x_n) grows linearly.

records.title: Status of other g (problem)
records.stmt: G=2,3,6 cannot be G_inf; P_g exists for gcd(g,6)=1; for 2|g or 3|g nothing proved (K10.6).
records.corr: Partly answered by F.T45 (g|24 impossible) and F.T46 (3|g allowed); even g beyond 24 still unclassified.

records.title: Elementary construction of P_g
records.stmt: For g>=5, gcd(g,6)=1, o=ord_g(2), s=(g+1)(g+2)^o, x0=s^2/g: x_n=s_n^2 t_n/g, G=g, x_{n+3}=4x_n for all n. Dirichlet not needed.
records.proof: Verifies H1-H3. Verified for 42 values of g; direct orbits g<=77.

records.title: Periodic increment of fibre size
records.stmt: In orbits satisfying T38 (or T46): R(x_n)=#{(a,j): a|m, 0<=j<=k_n, 2^j a=1 mod g}-1; k_{n+3o}=k_n+o; R(x_{n+3o})-R(x_n)=A_g(m).

records.title: The gamma-framework
records.stmt: (a) x=gamma L^2/g with gamma=gx/L^2 in N; (b) G=1 iff 4g | gamma L^2; (c) for a G-preserving step gamma'=(gamma+1)/r^2, r=L'/L (plateau: gamma+1); (d) congruence advance mod 8 / 3 / 24 for even g, 3|g, 6|g; (e) denominator b=g/gcd(g,gamma).
records.hyp: Valid for every orbit with D nonempty.

records.title: G_inf cannot divide 24
records.stmt: If g>1 divides 24 then no collective orbit is persistent at G=g; G_inf is not in {2,3,4,6,8,12,24}. Proof by prime-class argument and descent of gamma.

records.title: Persistent regimes with gcd(g,6)>1 (Theorem P*)
records.stmt: For odd g>=5 (3|g allowed), s=2^k m, H1-H3 and (H4): same conclusions as T38. Instances g=15,39,51,57,87.
records.corr: Corrects the F.T39/F.T41 remark that P needs gcd(g,6)=1 (erratum recorded in v008).

records.title: Persistent orbits live in a bounded gamma-window
records.stmt: In a persistent orbit with collapse modulus M (4g if L odd, g if L even): gamma_n<=2M for all large n.

records.title: Scaling question (M4a, M4b)
records.stmt: M4a: every x0 has n0 with x_{n+3}=4x_n; M4b: every orbit is eventually x=s^2 t/g, t in {1,2,3}. Proved only for G_inf=1 and for P_g, P*_g.
records.corr: Universal statements M4a/M4b FALSE; withdrawn in F.T58 (E1,E2,E3,E4) using F.T50 and F.T57.

records.title: The one-step law
records.stmt: For persistent x=gamma L^2/g, w=gamma+1, h=gcd(g,w), b'=g/h, sigma'=L prod p^{floor(v_p(w/h)/2)}: D(C(x))={d|sigma': d>=2, d=1 mod b'}; persistence iff all such d are 1 mod g; then gamma'=w/r^2.
records.hyp: Persistent orbit (G=g>1).
records.proof: Proved. Basis for the residue machine.

records.title: The eight-step theorem (G=11)
records.stmt: For S_k=2^2 3^{3+k} 5^4, x=tS_k^2/11: the orbit from 67500^2/11 satisfies x_{n+8}=9x_n (gamma-cycle 1..8, one 3-carry per 8 steps), R(x_{n+8})=R(x_n)+2; x_{n+3}/x_n takes eight values.
records.proof: Explicit hand proof; 160+ direct orbit steps exact.

records.title: Finite-state closure: every persistent orbit scales exactly
records.stmt: Class lemma plus closure principle: every persistent orbit is eventually class-periodic, hence x_{n+P}=rho^2 x_n with rho>=2. Every orbit of C eventually satisfies such a law (G_inf=1: P=3, rho=2).

records.title: The window theorem
records.stmt: g odd implies 2|L_n for all n and g does not divide gamma_n+1; every complete carry has M^2<g (g odd) or M^2<=4g (g even); gcd(M,g)=1. A q-carry needs g>q^2; finitely many carry sizes for given g.
records.hyp: Persistent orbit.

records.title: The absorption criterion
records.stmt: d is available at a step iff M(d)^2 | w; L'=L*r with r=lcm{M(d): M(d)^2 | w}. Types: none / partial / complete (complete implies gcd(g,w)=1).

records.title: Carry completeness
records.stmt: At a carry from a plateau that started at gamma_s: gamma'<=gamma_s/4+1; if gamma_s=1 then w=M^2=r^2 and gamma'=1. After finitely many carries gamma=1 and every carry is complete with cycle length M^2-1.

records.title: Eventual carries are prime powers
records.stmt: In the eventually periodic regime every carry M is a prime power p^j.

records.title: The decoupled odometer law
records.stmt: Active primes behave as independent counters e_p mod o_p; at gamma=1 the next carry is p^{j_p} for the active p minimising p^{j_p}, j_p=min{j>=1: (e_p+j) mod o_p in Abs_p}.
records.hyp: Multi-prime clause was untested in v009 (O9.2), resolved by F.T60.

records.title: General q-carry theorem
records.stmt: For odd prime q and odd prime g>q^2 with (Q1)-(Q4): gamma_n=(n mod (q^2-1))+1, x_{n+q^2-1}=q^2 x_n, R grows by 2 per carry. Instances q=3 (g=11), q=5 (g=31, 71), q=7 (g=367).
records.hyp: Hypotheses (Q1)-(Q4) finite-checkable; solvability for every q is OPEN (O9.1).

records.title: Corrections to v008
records.stmt: (E1) M4a FALSE (T50(iv), T57). (E2) M4b FALSE. (E3) x_{n+3}=4x_n iff gamma_{n+3}=4gamma_n/rho^2; separate gamma and L conditions are sufficient, not necessary. (E4) gamma-cycle is 1,...,M^2-1 with M the minimal available prime-power carry; M=2 gives 1,2,3. (E5) v008 T47 consistent.
records.corr: Corrects F.T48 and the v008 remark 'cycle 1,2,3 forced'.

records.title: The carry scheduler
records.stmt: At a reset state of the eventual regime the next carry is the prime p with the smallest pending carry c_p(E)=p^{j_p}; ties impossible; the orbit stays persistent iff c_p^2<g (g odd; <4g even).
records.hyp: Eventual regime of a persistent orbit.
records.proof: Restates T53-T56 as a dynamical system.

records.title: Single-prime dominance
records.stmt: In the eventual regime of every persistent orbit (every g, every seed) exactly one prime is active; no p!=q both carry infinitely often. Same for abstract odometer systems. Resolves O9.2 negatively. Corollaries: starvation rule; threshold-overlap condition vacuous; regime I is the p=2 case.
records.hyp: Proof does not use primality of g.
records.indep: The abstract statement (cyclic odometer systems with the minimum-pending-carry rule: at most one odometer fires infinitely often) is independent of C; its application to collective orbits needs F.T59.

records.title: The eventual scaling factor is a prime power
records.stmt: With one active prime p and minimal translation period s of Abs_p: P_gamma=sum(p^{2j_i}-1), L_{n+P_gamma}=p^s L_n, hence x_{n+P_gamma}=p^{2s}x_n. Every orbit eventually satisfies x_{n+P}=p^{2s}x_n with p prime.

records.title: Two saturated clocks have coprime periods
records.stmt: For odd prime g and saturated p!=q: Abs_p is tau_p-periodic, tau_p=o_p/gcd(o_p,o_q), similarly for q; tau_p and tau_q are coprime.
records.hyp: Prime g.
records.indep: Pure group theory of the cyclic group (Z/g)*, g odd prime: independent of C. It applies to collective orbits through the definition of Abs_p (F.T56).

records.title: Corrections to the v010 problem statement
records.stmt: (E1) threshold-overlap lemma true but not sharp (sharp form is T60). (E2) counter-rotating odometers cannot exist. (E3) coexistence classification: none, by proof.
records.corr: Itself the correction record for the v010 problem statement (not a result about C).

records.title: Exact carry-level predictor
records.stmt: From a reset state E (exact G=g), the next carry is M*=min{M>=2 available at E}; next state is again a reset state; carry occupies gamma-steps 1..M*^2-1; persistent through it iff M*^2<g (g odd prime; in general iff gcd(g,w)=1 for all w<=M*^2). After the first reset every state is a reset state.

records.title: Minimax selection theorem
records.stmt: For fixed independent odometers the survivor is p_*=argmin m_i, m_i=p_i^{d_i} (d_i largest cyclic gap of Abs_i), independent of phases; with window W the system stays admissible iff m_{p_*}<W.
records.hyp: Fixed odometer tables (abstract setting); not by itself the collective map (see T66).
records.indep: The whole statement is about fixed independent odometers (abstract setting) and is independent of C; it describes a collective orbit only via F.T56/F.T59, and v011 itself notes it does not by itself apply to the collective map.

records.title: Quotient-residue formula
records.stmt: Abs_p={k mod o_p: k mod t_p in S_p}, S_p={r mod t_p: p^r f in H for some f in F}; m_p=p^{maxgap(S_p)}; for prime g, t_p=o_p/gcd(o_p,|H|). Also valid for composite g (plain order).
records.indep: The quotient formula is a statement about residues in (Z/g)* and holds for any g; the objects Abs_p, H, F come from collective orbits (F.T56, F.T66).

records.title: Static survivor certificate
records.stmt: Under S3 (m^2<g), S4 (no available M<m coprime to r), S5 (no prime factor of g <= m^2) at a reset state with r saturated: only r carries forever, x_{n+P}=r^{2s}x_n for all n>=0. Necessity holds for prime g. At most one prime is certified. Unsaturated extension T66'.
records.hyp: g prime, or no prime factor of g <= m^2; E a reset state with G=g exactly.
records.corr: Scope of the general phrasing restricted in F.T73 (E12.1).

records.title: Consequences of static certification
records.stmt: (a) every persistent orbit reaches a statically certified reset state; (b) future determined by finite data; (c) g alone does not determine the survivor.
records.hyp: (a) as worded for 'every persistent orbit'.
records.corr: (a) corrected by F.T73 (E12.1): proved for PRIME g only; composite/even g fail S5 in all six tested cycles.

records.title: Reset-descent bound (sharp)
records.stmt: In a constant-G segment from gamma_0, the first reset occurs after at most kappa(gamma_0) carries (kappa = iterations of f(a)=floor(a/4)+1); kappa(a)=least k with 4^k>(3a-4)/2; attained for every kappa=1..11 (e.g. g=79, gamma_0=1444161: 11).
records.hyp: Constant-G segment; any g.
records.proof: Proved; attained witnesses re-run by exact iteration of C. Registry recheck: kappa(2,10,100,1000,10^6)=1,2,4,6,11 and the closed form hold for all a<=300000.
records.indep: The function kappa and the descent a -> floor(a/4)+1 are pure arithmetic (checked for all a <= 300000 in this registry); the carry-count statement for constant-G segments is scope C.

records.title: Class-counting entry bound
records.stmt: After the first reset the class sequence repeats within H(g)=prod_{p^2<g}(2o_p-1) steps; cycle entered at index i<=H(g)-1; for prime g the entry state is statically certified. Carries to a certified state <= kappa(gamma_0)+H(g)-1.
records.hyp: (c) certification for prime g (or whenever T66 applies).
records.proof: Proved. Registry recheck: H(11)=171, H(31)=2655, H(59)=21297195.

records.title: Polynomial entry bound
records.stmt: Entry/exit index <= K_poly(g)=(Phi+1)(Sigma+(Sigma+1)(omega+1)+1), cubic in the orders, via scheduler epochs (lemmas L1, L2, potential Phi).
records.hyp: g prime, or whenever T67 applies.
records.corr: Post-freeze numerical erratum F.E71 (registry, approved): the data sentence in THEOREMS.md T71 quotes 'H~10^15, K_poly~2*10^8' for g=211; the exact values are H(211)=2.4e13, K_poly(211)=1.14e8 (RESULTS.md has them right; the quoted figures match g=197). Theorem and proof unaffected.

records.title: Dynamic-G effective bound
records.stmt: From any state: chain of segments g_0>g_1>...>g_k>=1; at most Omega(g_0) segments with G>1; gamma_{i+1}<=g_{i+1}(gamma_i+4g_i+1)/g_i; segment carries <= kappa(gamma_i)+H(g_i)-1; G=1 tail <=4*kappa_3(t) steps; explicit total R(g_0,gamma_0).
records.hyp: Bound uses T71/T70 for segments; explicit but astronomically loose.
records.proof: Proved. Exact total transient time is NOT given.

records.title: Registered corrections and scope (v012)
records.stmt: (E12.1) v011 T68(a) is proved for prime g only; for g=15,39,51,57,68,87 every reset state fails S5. (E12.2) proposal's T69 loses a factor 2 per carry. (E12.3) entry index <=H-1. (E12.4) dynamic-G bound is explicit but the exact transient time remains open.
records.corr: Corrects F.T68.

records.title: Exact transient time / near-sharp bound
records.stmt: An exact transient time or a bound within a small factor of the observed entry index (observed <=208 for g=211 vs bounds >=10^8). Route in source: bound the epochs actually used, or bound non-survivor firings via the m_p ordering.

records.title: Static certificate for composite/even g
records.stmt: Replace hypothesis S5 of T66 by a condition on the plateau steps with gcd(g,w)>1 so that certification works for composite/even g.

records.title: T71 where T67 does not apply
records.stmt: Polynomial entry bound for composite g outside the scope of the carry-level predictor.

records.title: Closed-form m_p and survivor for q-carry families
records.stmt: Closed form of the worst-case carry m_p and of the survivor from (g,q) alone.

records.title: Infinitely many carry sizes
records.stmt: Whether (Q1)-(Q4) of T57 are solvable for every odd prime q (11 exact instances q<=37 recorded in v012). Chebotarev/Kummer argument plausible, not carried out.

records.title: q=11 class-closure certificate (g=6689)
records.stmt: The class-closure certificate for q=11, g=6689 is incomplete (about 50,000 machine steps needed).

records.title: Realisable triples (g, p, Abs_p)
records.stmt: Which triples (g,p,Abs_p) are realisable by seeds; T62 and the window c^2<g restrict them; complete characterisation not given.

records.title: Composite/even g sample
records.stmt: T59-T60 do not use primality of g, but the numerical sample is almost entirely prime g.

records.title: Fibre classification, R-growth rate, branch comparison
records.stmt: Compound record (v004 problems still open after v005 closed J1 and v005 T33 answered 'does every d enter D'). [A0] full list of primitive configurations of rigid three-route fibres (pure fibre arithmetic, no interaction choice). [C] true growth rate of R(x_n) along collective orbits. [X] finer structural comparison of the route-aware and collective branches (problem J4).

records.title: SELECT-I: justification of E, T_q status, retention
records.stmt: Independent justification of E (amplification as a generative step), of treating T_q as a symmetry rather than a step, and of retention as a requirement (nest iteration consumes factors).

records.title: SELECT-II: closed-form criterion for m ~> t
records.stmt: Number-theoretic (non-recursive) necessary and sufficient condition for m to reach t.
records.release: SELECT-II v002b — Complete Histories and Confluence

records.title: SELECT-II: double-confluence pattern and Min C(a,b)
records.stmt: Pattern of the 9 double-confluence pairs; systematic computation of the set-valued minimal common successors Min C(a,b) and whether it yields a relational deficit.

records.title: SELECT-II: retrospective invariants vs D
records.stmt: Whether any natural retrospective invariant (merge geometry, common-ancestor structure) is non-trivially related to the manuscript distance D.

records.title: Post-freeze numerical erratum to the T71 data sentence
records.stmt: The data clause 'against H ~ 10^15 and K_poly ~ 2*10^8' (attached to g=211) is replaced by 'against H(211) ~ 2.4*10^13 and K_poly(211) ~ 1.1*10^8'. Only these two numerical expressions change; see ERRATA/ERRATUM_F.T71_v012_numerical.md for the exact original and corrected reading.
records.hyp: Data clause only. T71's statement, hypotheses (g prime, or whenever T67 applies) and proof are unchanged.
records.proof: Values recomputed from the definitions (H(211)=24165141422031, K_poly(211)=113903360) and supported by v012 RESULTS.md.
records.corr: Registered post-freeze; frozen v012 (commit bb8b12d) is NOT overwritten. Cite the original commit together with this erratum.
